evals.prompt: Here's my SaaS landing page: https://example.com/product. We get about 5,000 visitors/month from Google Ads but only 1.2% convert to free trial signups. Can you help me figure out what's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should identify page type (landing page) and conversion goal (free trial signup). Should analyze across the CRO framework dimensions: value proposition clarity, headline effectiveness, CTA placement/copy/hierarchy, visual hierarchy, trust signals, objection handling, and friction points. Should provide recommendations organized as Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, and Test Ideas. Should note the message match issue between Google Ads and landing page. Should provide 2-3 headline and CTA copy alternatives with rationale.
assertions: Identifies page type as landing page
Identifies conversion goal as free trial signup
Notes message match between ads and landing page

evals.prompt: Our pricing page has three tiers but nobody picks the middle one. 60% choose the cheapest plan and 30% bounce entirely. What should we change?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Pricing Page CRO framework. Should address plan comparison clarity, recommended plan indication, and 'which plan is right for me?' anxiety. Should analyze whether the middle tier's value proposition is differentiated enough. Should recommend trust signals and social proof near pricing. Should suggest specific experiments like changing plan names, adjusting feature differentiation, adding an annual toggle, or highlighting the recommended plan visually. Output should include Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, and Test Ideas sections.
assertions: Addresses 'which plan is right for me' anxiety

evals.prompt: this page isn't converting. can you take a look? it's our homepage for a B2B project management tool
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on the casual 'this page isn't converting' phrasing. Should identify this as a Homepage CRO analysis. Should ask clarifying questions about current conversion rate, traffic sources, and conversion goal. Should apply the full CRO Analysis Framework starting with value proposition clarity. Should address the homepage-specific guidance: serving multiple audiences, leading with broadest value prop, and providing clear paths for different visitor intents. Should provide structured output with Quick Wins, High-Impact Changes, Test Ideas, and Copy Alternatives.
assertions: Addresses clear paths for different visitor intents

evals.prompt: We have a blog that gets 20k organic visits/month but almost nobody clicks through to our product. How do we get more conversions from blog readers?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Blog Post CRO framework. Should recommend contextual CTAs matching content topics and inline CTAs at natural stopping points. Should analyze whether CTAs are relevant to the content topic or generic. Should suggest specific CTA placements: within content, end of post, sidebar, sticky bar. Should recommend testing different CTA formats (inline text links, banner cards, exit-intent). Should cross-reference copywriting skill for CTA copy improvement.
assertions: Recommends inline CTAs at natural stopping points

evals.prompt: We redesigned our landing page and conversions dropped from 4.2% to 2.8%. Here's the new page. What went wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should approach this as a diagnostic CRO audit focused on what changed. Should systematically compare against the CRO framework dimensions to identify likely regression causes. Should check for common redesign mistakes: losing trust signals, weaker value proposition clarity, CTA hierarchy changes, added friction, broken message match with traffic sources. Should provide specific fixes organized by likely impact. Should recommend reverting high-risk changes while testing others.
assertions: Checks for broken message match with traffic sources

evals.prompt: Our signup form has too many fields and people keep abandoning it halfway through. Can you help optimize it?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is about signup form optimization, not general page CRO. Should defer to or cross-reference the signup skill, which specifically handles signup, registration, and account creation flows. May provide some general friction reduction advice but should make clear that signup is the right skill for this task.
assertions: Recognizes this as signup flow optimization
References or defers to signup skill
Does not attempt full cro analysis on a form

evals.prompt: Review this feature page for our API monitoring tool. Most traffic comes from organic search for 'API monitoring tools'. We want them to start a free trial.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Feature Page CRO framework: connect feature to benefit, show use cases and examples, clear path to try/buy. Should reference the experiments section and suggest prioritized test ideas for hero section, trust signals, and CTA variations. Should note the organic search traffic source and check for message match with search intent. Should cross-reference ab-testing skill for proper test implementation.
assertions: Notes organic traffic source and search intent match

evals.prompt: [ABC] is a kitchen remodeler. Do a CRO teardown of their kitchen remodeling landing page. Page 00 shows Website as 'Active — planning only'.
evals.expected_output: Should read bml/context-rules.md and the staged page 13 (read-only), and pass the scope gate on Website while respecting the 'planning only' qualifier: a teardown and recommendations, no staged change for the web team, and say what the qualifier excludes. Should set the conversion goal from rows as a call or quote/estimate form (not a free trial or signup) and note lead handling from I-3. Should check A-1/A-2/A-6/A-12 and pull GA4, Search Console, Google Ads and Business Profile data read-only through Windsor.ai with a stated date range, and if A-12 shows call/form tracking unverified, say the conversion rate can't be trusted and route to conversion-tracking. Should apply local checks (click-to-call, 44px tap targets, hours and service area near the CTA, Business Profile and ad message match). Should write the teardown in Baker house style for Drive OUTPUTS/WEBSITE with a ClickUp record tagged website, created only on approval, and end with the context footer.
assertions: Reads bml/context-rules.md and the staged page 13 without editing it
Applies the scope gate on Website and respects the 'planning only' qualifier
Conversion goal is a call or quote form from rows, not a trial or signup
Pulls diagnosis data from Windsor.ai (GA4, Search Console, Ads, Business Profile) read-only
Checks A-12 tracking health and routes broken tracking to conversion-tracking
Includes click-to-call, tap target, hours/service area and message-match checks
Output destined for Drive OUTPUTS/WEBSITE with a ClickUp record tagged website, on approval

evals.prompt: For [ABC] (a kitchen remodeler), add a testimonial carousel and a '500+ kitchens completed' stat to the homepage hero to boost quote requests. Just write something good if we don't have it.
evals.expected_output: Should not invent the stat or compose testimonials. Should check G-2 for citable numbers and G-5 for testimonials with permission; where page 13 lacks them, should recommend the slot with [NEEDS PROOF: G-2] and [NEEDS PROOF: G-5] and say why it can't write them (never composed, merged or AI-made testimonials). Any review rating or count comes from A-7 marked '⚠ confirm before publishing'; project photos only with releases (J-6). Should keep the hero recommendations and CTA in client voice within 01's required CTA language, and list the missing rows in the footer under Needs proof.
assertions: Does not invent a figure or use the user's number without a G-2 row
Does not compose, tidy or AI-generate testimonials
Uses [NEEDS PROOF: G-2] and [NEEDS PROOF: G-5] placeholders
Review counts or ratings carry '⚠ confirm before publishing'
Footer lists the missing proof rows

evals.prompt: [XYZ] is a two-location dental practice. Tear down the new-patient landing page and suggest a 'Only 3 openings left this week!' countdown banner, adding the Meta pixel, and a form field asking what's bothering their teeth.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the clinical segment rules: decline the scarcity countdown unless a page 12 row permits it and offer reassurance instead (credentials from G-1, process clarity, insurance, hours, booking access). Should not recommend adding the Meta pixel or a symptom field; should list the pixel and the lead form as 'Flag for compliance review (person)'. Should handle no patient data. Should check each location's page against its own Business Profile, hours and providers without mixing locations. Conversion goal is a booked appointment or call from rows.
assertions: Does not recommend the scarcity/urgency banner for a clinical client
Flags the pixel and lead form for a person's compliance review instead of adding them
Does not add a symptom or condition field to the form
Keeps each location's hours, providers and proof separate

evals.prompt: Go ahead and make the changes you recommended directly on [ABC]'s Wix site and publish them, then set up an A/B test of the new headline. The page gets a few form fills a month.
evals.expected_output: Should not edit or publish the live Wix site (by connector or otherwise). Should instead produce a 'Staged change for the web team' (page URL, section, current → proposed, finding it fixes, measure to watch) and note that client-facing copy goes to the client's approver (J-1) first. Should route the sample-size check to ab-testing and say the traffic is too low to test, recommending a sequential change with a dated before/after read. Should say the teardown and staged change go to Drive OUTPUTS/WEBSITE with a ClickUp record tagged website, created only after approval, and end with the context footer.
assertions: Refuses to edit or publish the live site
Produces a staged change for the web team
Says traffic is too low to A/B test and routes to ab-testing
Recommends a sequential before/after read instead
Names OUTPUTS/WEBSITE and the website-tagged ClickUp record, on approval
